text:
Jeremy Swayman made 40 saves, and Boston needed every one of them to stretch its winning streak to four games. The Bruins scored three times in the first 16 minutes at TD Garden, the first on a chance our numbers gave only a 4% shot at going in, and held off a Florida team that spent most of the night in their end. Swayman, drafted 111th overall in 2017 and a University of Maine goalie as recently as 2019-20, was named first star.

The scoreboard and the play did not match. Florida generated 3.79 expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, to Boston's 3.56, and our simulation of every shot says the Panthers deserved to win 54% of the time. Swayman faced shots worth 3.79 goals and let in one, saving 2.79 more than an average goalie would have. Brady Tkachuk put eight shots on goal, and his best look, a 23% chance in the first period, was stopped by Swayman. The Panthers also outshot Boston 41 to 36 and outhit them 38 to 13, but won only 28 of 77 faceoffs.

Boston's goals came off finishing rather than volume. Elias Lindholm and Michael Eyssimont scored 76 seconds apart early, Morgan Geekie added a power-play slap shot, and JJ Peterka made it 4-1 less than a minute into the third. David Pastrnak had two assists and Pavel Zacha two more. Carter Verhaeghe's power-play goal with 1:55 left in the first was all Florida got past Swayman. The Bruins carry four straight wins out of this one. For the Panthers, it is a night where the chances were there and the result was not.
